episode_title: Be the Expert. Build the Business: Interview with Wilson Harwood

real_qa.q: When should sound isolation acoustic consultants be brought into the design phase of a building project?
real_qa.r: In an ideal situation, bringing on the isolation acoustic professional during the initial design phase is important because sound isolation work is structural. Making choices early—such as building on a concrete slab versus the second level of a home with wood deck construction—can save a client thousands or tens of thousands of dollars, whereas being brought in late forces reactive design fixes rather than proactive collaboration.
real_qa.requete: sound isolation consultant early design phase

real_qa.q: What is the difference between sound isolation and room acoustics in building design?
real_qa.r: Sound isolation is keeping sound in and out of spaces, while room acoustics is improving the sound quality within a room. For example, an echoey restaurant where conversation is difficult is an acoustics problem solved by acoustic panels in the ceiling. Sound isolation, by contrast, blocks external or internal sounds from entering or leaving a space—crucial for neurodivergent individuals sensitive to low frequencies or people requiring acoustic privacy.
real_qa.requete: sound isolation versus room acoustics difference

real_qa.q: How can construction checklists improve acoustic design execution on job sites?
real_qa.r: Checklists organized by construction phases and cross-referenced to plan sections help builders understand the chronological order of critical acoustic details, making non-traditional construction less intimidating. Paired with photo and video documentation uploaded to Google Drive and labeled to specific plan sections, checklists create layers of verification that prevent small mistakes—which are significant in sound isolation work—without requiring constant on-site presence.
real_qa.requete: construction checklists acoustic design site execution

real_qa.q: Why is white noise an ineffective solution for sound isolation in offices and professional spaces?
real_qa.r: White noise is a Band-Aid fix that may slightly disrupt speech traveling through a door but adds more noise back into the environment. More critically, white noise cannot stop low-frequency sounds or bass, which pass through it easily; since stopping bass is the hardest part of sound isolation work, white noise fails to address the most challenging acoustic problems.
real_qa.requete: white noise sound isolation ineffective why

real_qa.q: What building envelope and structural elements does SPYS Designs address beyond interior drywall in sound isolation projects?
real_qa.r: Sound isolation begins at the outside of a building, not just the interior. Exterior walls both internally and on the building's outside require careful design, often involving non-traditional layers of sheathing. Additionally, details around how electrical, HVAC, and other mechanical systems penetrate through walls into the interior can compromise acoustics if not properly specified and executed.
real_qa.requete: building envelope exterior walls sound isolation design

guest.bio_context: Wilson Harwood is an acoustician specializing in sound isolation design for residential projects including home recording studios, hi-fi listening rooms, and home theaters. He has developed expertise in the structural and technical aspects of sound isolation, often being brought into projects to address acoustic requirements that extend beyond basic architectural knowledge.
